ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit 3e2d300ad331d7dfd63f399486154edd370a07aa, frozen before any rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are the same-plugin siblings prototype:explore-directions (throwaway, structurally different UI layouts of one screen behind a switcher) and prototype:build-generator (a tunable throwaway generator for an artifact prompting cannot hit). pressure-test owns building a throwaway, hand-driven model of business rules, a state machine, a data model or an API surface to see what it does with awkward cases before committing to it.

queries.request: If a customer cancels while the warehouse is already packing, and the courier picks it up anyway, what do our order rules end up doing? I'd like to click through it.
Throw together a quick terminal toy so I can poke at our seat-reservation rules: hold, release, expire, double-book.
Can a ticket go straight from closed back to in progress under the workflow we drafted? Let me drive it step by step before we build it.
I'm not sure our proposed invoice record can represent a split payment across two cards. Build something throwaway so I can try it with weird examples.
Before we lock the public interface for the scheduler, I want to play with a draft of the calls, by job id or by name, in a scratch harness.
Our loan rules allow two renewals, but nobody knows what happens when someone else has a hold on the book. Make a small interactive model I can step through.
Turn the subscription lifecycle into a clickable HTML page the product manager can operate with buttons, no terminal needed.
Sketch the coupon stacking rules as a disposable CLI so I can feed it odd combinations and watch the totals change.
What do our inventory reservation rules do when a restock lands between two partial shipments? Spin up a scratch app to find out.
I want to try our draft refund policy against strange orderings of events interactively before anyone writes production code.
Show me three different ways the subscription billing page could be laid out so the team can pick one.
Help me decide the types and module boundaries for the new fulfillment package before I write the implementation plan.
Write unit tests for the existing refund calculator, covering partial refunds and currency rounding.
Orders got stuck in pending after payment succeeded in production last night. Figure out why it's broken.
Draw an ERD of our tables from the Prisma schema so I can see which entities relate to which.
What should the returns screen look like? Give me a few clickable mockups to flip between.
We need to handle late refunds better somehow. List some approaches we could take, from cheapest to most ambitious.
Add property-based tests to the booking module so CI catches invalid status transitions.
Moving an order from shipped to returned throws an exception for some customers. Debug it.
Settle the domain types for loyalty points (balances, accruals, expiries) and the contract the checkout service will call, so I can plan the work.
